title: User management
description: Create, delete, disable users; change passwords; preferences and configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first. `compat/captures/users-admin-12.4.md` and `.json`, from a script under `test/differential/`, with an admin and two viewers: `GET /Users` with and without `isHidden` and `isDisabled`; `POST /Users/New`: a name already used in other case, an empty name, no password; `POST /Users?userId=`; `DELETE /Users/{id}`: self, last admin, a user nobody has, a malformed id; `POST /Users/{id}/Policy`: the full body, missing fields, demoting the last admin, disabling yourself; `POST /Users/Password`: wrong, empty and right `CurrentPw`; an admin for another user; `ResetPassword`; a user with no password; `GET /Auth/Providers` and `/Auth/PasswordResetProviders`; a disabled user's sign-in and token; every request jellyfin-web 12.4's user list, new-user, profile, parental-control, password and Quick Connect pages send, and what each page shows for a 400 or 403 from them.

The 12.4 routes answer with the status and shape captured: `POST /Users/New`, `GET /Users`, `POST /Users`, `DELETE /Users/{userId}`, `POST /Users/{userId}/Policy`, `POST /Users/Password`, `GET /Auth/Providers` (and `/Auth/PasswordResetProviders` if the pages call it). Every difference goes in `compat/differences.yaml`. POST /Users/{userId}/Password, which jellyfin-web calls and Jellyfin marks obsolete, is an alias (compat/captures/users-admin-12.4.md, invariant 20, D-069).

`Route.Access` gains `admin`, and `Handler()` still panics on any other word. Five routes declare it with `Users: admin-any`: `POST /Users/New`, `DELETE /Users/{userId}`, `POST /Users/{userId}/Policy` and `GET /Auth/Providers` and `GET /Auth/PasswordResetProviders` (Jellyfin refuses viewers both). On each, a viewer token gets 403, and no token or an unknown one gets 401 (401 first), with no statement beyond the token lookup. TestAccess asks each. Named mutant: the guard treating admin as viewer. A viewer's request with a malformed id on an admin route is 403, as captured: access is checked before the id.

`GET /Users`, `POST /Users` and `POST /Users/Password` are viewer routes with `Users: admin-any`, through JS-127's one helper: a non-admin naming someone else or nobody gets 403, and nothing is read; an admin naming nobody gets 404; a malformed id gets 400; path and query disagreeing gets 400 for an admin. The pull request lists the larger admin-any set; `endpoints.yaml` and `docs/access.md` are regenerated with `user:`.

`GET /Users` gives a viewer exactly one entry, themselves, and an admin every user, disabled ones included, each with its stored IsAdministrator and IsDisabled. In a recorded jellyfin-web run, the Quick Connect page lists every enabled user to an admin.

`POST /Users/New` makes an enabled non-admin. A name taken in any case gets the captured answer, and nothing is created. Forced: two processes creating one name at once make exactly one user. A deleted user's name can be reused; the new user inherits no watch state, favourite, device or token.

Enforced Policy: changes to IsAdministrator, IsDisabled and EnableContentDownloading act on the next request through another process. A demoted admin gets 403 on the admin routes. With EnableContentDownloading false, GET /Items/{id}/Download is 403 through stream, and that user's item says CanDownload false, decided per user at answer time and never written into the shared items.dto. LoginAttemptsBeforeLockout stays -1, no account is disabled by failed sign-ins, and a POST changing LoginAttemptsBeforeLockout or InvalidLoginAttemptCount from GET's value is 400 (D-020, D-093).

Policy says only what is enforced: IsAdministrator, IsDisabled and EnableContentDownloading are stored and act. A POST changing any other field from the value GET answers is 400 naming every such field, stores nothing, and is logged at warn with the user and the fields. Not a change: null where GET answers []; any value of EnableAllChannels, EnabledChannels or BlockedChannels (no channels exist; listed in compat/differences.yaml). GET's own Policy posted back answers 204 (D-093).

A disabled user's right password gets the wrong password's 401 byte for byte, after the same bcrypt work, shown by a timing check that can fail (as JS-145). A deleted user's name answers as an unknown name, and counts toward the JS-145 bounds like one. The log names the disabled account as the reason (D-096). Re-enabling brings back no old token, as Jellyfin 12.4 does.

Forced with real processes (`test/roles.sh`): after a disable or delete through api 1, every token of the user gets 401 on its next `GET /Users/Me` through api 2 and its next byte range and HLS segment through stream.

After a disable or delete commits and the stream replica's next snapshot refresh (5 s or less), with Postgres held away, the user's byte ranges are not served from the snapshot. Invariant 37's accepted window covers only a change in the 5 s before an outage.

Quick Connect (JS-037): a disabled account's Authorize is 401. A code it approved, redeemed through another process after the disable or delete commits, gives the unknown-secret 404 and issues no token. `quickconnect.Redeem` checks only that the user exists today.

The last-admin race as written: demote, disable, delete, and a mixed pair (A demotes B while B deletes A). Exactly one 204, the other 403, and one enabled admin remains. Named mutant as written. A sole admin doing any of the three to themselves gets 403.
Delete removes the user's `user_item_data`, `display_preferences`, `devices`, `sessions`, `session_sockets` and approved Quick Connect codes in one transaction, and no row of another user changes.

Passwords: Changing your own needs the current one. A wrong one changes nothing and counts in JS-145's per-name and per-address bounds together with sign-in; 10 from one address gets 403 with Retry-After. A user with no password follows D-105. An admin resets another's password without the current one. Either way, the user's other tokens get 401 on the next request through api 2 and stream; the device that changed its own password keeps its token.
A new or changed password in the shipped list is 400 with a message, and nothing is stored. `docs/access.md` names the list's source and size, and nothing is sent outside the operator's servers.

A running stream stops: forced, a direct play of the whole file read slowly closes within 15 s of sign-out, a password change, delete or disable, having sent less than the file. An HLS viewer's next segment gets 401.

In the jellyfin-web e2e tier an admin lists, creates, sets a password, disables, enables, demotes and deletes; the profile, password, parental-control and access pages save, and delete works; New User works with 'all libraries' ticked. Otherwise, until JS-036, it makes the user and shows its generic error (D-093).
Criterion 11 kept: LoginAttemptsBeforeLockout stays -1 and the `differences.yaml` entry stands (D-020).

A Policy POST changes only the fields its body names: omitting IsAdministrator, IsDisabled or EnableContentDownloading leaves each as stored (Jellyfin resets them; listed in compat/differences.yaml); a body without the provider ids is accepted (D-094).

While adminUser names a user, DELETE and a name change of that user answer 403 naming the adminUser key, logged at warn; with the key removed they are an ordinary user's. Demote and disable are allowed and survive a restart. docs/running.md says so (D-095).

Start-up that would create adminUser with a commonly guessed JELLYSCALE_ADMIN_PASSWORD stops, naming the variable and never the value; an existing account is never checked, so no upgrade stops. The quick start's example password changes (D-095). If the test fixtures need more than a password swap, the lead returns to the product owner.

Settled at Check (lead): an administrator naming the zero id gets JS-127's 404 (Jellyfin's 400 is listed in compat/differences.yaml); disabling an administrator stays allowed under the last-administrator rule, and Jellyfin's refusal is listed there (D-095); a wrong CurrentPw counts toward the requesting device's bound as a known device and toward the per-address bound (D-020).

An empty new password is refused like a commonly guessed one: 400 with the reason in the body, nothing stored, whoever sets it (listed in compat/differences.yaml; jellyfin-web shows its generic message, and docs/access.md says so). An administrator's ResetPassword of another user leaves the account with no password: every password sign-in for it, the empty one included, gets the wrong password's 401 until an administrator sets one, and every token of the user gets 401 on its next request through api 2 and stream. Other sign-ins (D-102) are unaffected. A ResetPassword of one's own account is refused and changes nothing, administrator or not, with or without CurrentPw. (D-100, D-103).

An account with no password (migrated, created without one, or reset by an administrator) is refused every password sign-in, the empty password included, with the wrong password's 401 after the same bcrypt work, until an administrator sets a password; its other sign-ins (D-102) are unaffected. POST /Users/New with no or an empty Password creates the user with no password (listed in compat/differences.yaml). docs/access.md and JS-060's migration docs tell the operator to set each such user's password or link them through the provider (D-105).

Settled at Check (lead): the pages' other calls work: GET /Channels and GET /Localization/ParentalRatings answer a valid empty list, and GET /Library/MediaFolders and GET /Devices answer minimal real lists with admin access, each only if a page the criteria name needs it; compat/differences.yaml keeps the IsHidden entry, citing D-093 and no task; every fixture and test that configures a commonly guessed admin password swaps it (D-095).

No token outlives a disable: sign-in, Quick Connect redemption and a password change cannot leave a live token for an account being disabled, forced with the disable held (D-096, criterion on disabled accounts).

Stopping a running stream costs Postgres no more than a poll: forced, a slow direct play of 15 seconds adds at most a handful of statements on the stream replica, not one per chunk sent (invariant 10).
notes: /Configuration moved to JS-116 (2026-11-15). Access criteria from the access model (2026-11-16). Refine with care: a throttle per client address needs a trusted-proxy setting first (behind an ingress every request has its address), and a lockout by user name lets anyone lock a known account out. State what start-up does when the configured administrator was deleted or demoted through the API. D-069: named mutants are shown failing once by hand in the Spec step and recorded in the task's record; no mutant table or script is committed.
